title: Understanding the Minimum Wage 18 Year Old Victoria: Hourly to Annual Pay Guide
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual salary with our guide. Learn about the minimum wage 18 year old victoria, tax, super, and the 38-hour week. Use our timesheet for accurate calcul
salarySummary: For a full-time employee on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, working 38 hours per week, the annual gross pay is approximately $52,253.44.

faqs.q: What is the minimum wage for an 18-year-old in Victoria?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage for adults is $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026. However, for 18-year-olds covered by a modern award, junior rates apply as a percentage of the adult award rate. Check the Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides for your specific award.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by your weekly hours (typically 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,253.44 per year. Our [timesheet](/) tool does this automatically.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how is it applied?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of leave entitlements. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour. Our [timesheet](/) has a checkbox to add casual loading.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Salary

If you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, the simplest way to compare them is to convert one to the other. The formula is straightforward: **annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For full-time employees, the standard week is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Act. If you are unsure of your weekly hours, 38 is a safe assumption for a full-time role.

For example, if you earn the **minimum wage 18 year old victoria** (which may be a junior rate under a modern award), you would use that hourly figure in the formula. But note that the National Minimum Wage for adults is $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026. For a 38-hour week, that gives $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.90 per week, and $1,004.90 × 52 = $52,253.44 per year. If you are paid fortnightly, simply double the weekly amount: $2,009.80 per fortnight.

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and automatically calculates the annual, weekly, and fortnightly figures. There is also a checkbox to add 25% casual loading on top of your base rate. Do **not** enter a rate that already includes casual loading; the tool adds it for you.

## The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour for adults, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making the casual rate $33.05 per hour. However, many employees are covered by a modern award or an enterprise agreement, which may set higher minimum rates. For example, the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) for an 18-year-old in Victoria under a retail or hospitality award is often a percentage of the adult award rate. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award, detailing junior rates, penalty rates, and allowances.

It is important to distinguish between the National Minimum Wage and award rates. The National Minimum Wage applies only to employees not covered by an award or agreement. If you are covered by an award, your minimum pay is the award rate, which is usually higher. Always check your award or agreement to confirm your correct minimum wage.

## Tax and Superannuation

Once you have your annual gross pay, you can estimate your take-home pay after tax and the super guarantee. The Australian Taxation Office's 2026–27 resident tax rates are:

- Nil on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds, as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). For a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage ($52,253.44), the estimated tax would be approximately $5,092 plus Medicare levy of $1,045, leaving about $46,116 take-home pay. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for a more detailed estimate.

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid **on top** of your salary. For the same worker, that would be $52,253.44 × 12% = $6,270.41 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional contribution your employer makes to your super fund. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for more.

## Important Considerations

Our annual pay calculation assumes the same hourly rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It is an estimate, not a determination of your actual pay. Casual loading is added separately via the checkbox on our [timesheet](/) – never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

For the **minimum wage 18 year old victoria**, remember that junior rates under awards vary. The Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog) are the authoritative source. You can also refer to our [reference tables](/data) for state and industry averages, but these are averages, not your job's median.

If you are comparing a salary offer to an hourly rate, use the formula above. Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page provides more examples. And if you are a casual worker, our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how the 25% loading works.

Finally, note that the Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes average weekly earnings. For Victoria, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,041.10 per week in May 2026. This is an average, not a median for your specific job. Use our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page to see national averages.

## Using Our Timesheet

Our [timesheet](/) is the home page. Simply type your base hourly rate (before any casual loading) and the tool will show your annual, weekly, and fortnightly gross pay. Check the box for casual loading if applicable. The tool uses the 38-hour week assumption by default, but you can adjust the hours per week if needed. It also provides a rough tax estimate using the 2026–27 rates and Medicare levy. Remember, this is an estimate only – consult a tax professional for your individual situation.
